strategy.summary: Reproduce numpy PR #25877: matrix_rank ignores batch broadcasting of a non-scalar rtol for stacked inputs. The developer's parametrized test in numpy/linalg/tests/test_regression.py calls matrix_rank(np.zeros((4,3,2)), rtol=rtol) for rtol in 0.0, [0.0]*4, np.zeros((4,)) and asserts result shape (4,). On the buggy revision 567b57d751fb the array-valued rtol cases should fail the shape assertion (or raise a broadcasting error inside the tolerance computation); on the fixed revision all cases pass. Build NumPy from source at the buggy commit, then run the single test with pytest.

system_packages: gcc or clang with C/C++ toolchain
BLAS/LAPACK is optional (NumPy wheels-free source build uses bundled OpenBLAS via scipy-openblas if available, otherwise system lapack)
build_commands: git checkout <fixed-parent-of-PR-25877-merge>  # then rebuild with pip install -e . --no-build-isolation to verify fix

strategy.reproducing_test: numpy/linalg/tests/test_regression.py::TestRegression::test_matrix_rank_rtol_argument (parametrized over rtol in [0.0, [0.0]*4, np.zeros((4,))]) with body: x = np.zeros((4,3,2)); res = np.linalg.matrix_rank(x, rtol=rtol); assert res.shape == (4,)
strategy.success_criterion: On buggy revision 567b57d751fb the test fails: at least the array-valued rtol parameterizations ([0.0]*4 and np.zeros((4,))) do not produce shape (4,) and the assertion fails (or an exception from mismatched broadcasting occurs). On the fixed revision (the PR merge with broadcast_to(rtol, A.shape[:-2])[..., newaxis]) all three parameterizations pass with result shape (4,).
strategy.numerical_probe: Not required by the transition; only the shape assertion is graded.

input_output_examples.input: x = np.zeros((4, 3, 2)) with rtol given as 0.0, [0.0]*4, or np.zeros((4,))

risks: Test file numpy/linalg/tests/test_regression.py may be named differently at buggy commit; the diff shows it exists there, so verify the class name (TestRegression) before selecting with -k.
The buggy-revision failure mode for the scalar rtol=0.0 case is expected to pass; only array rtol cases should transition. Do not treat a passing scalar case as a reproduction failure.
Exact numerical rank values are not in the evidence; the test checks shape only, so the transition depends on shape behaviour, not on values.
Intermediate fix using asarray(rtol)[..., newaxis] differs from final broadcast_to version; reproduce against the final merged fix, not an intermediate commit.
Build is required for a compiled NumPy; a wheel install of the released version will not contain the buggy code path. Build time may be long and needs a working C compiler and meson.
No platform-specific or sanitizer dependency is evidenced; the behaviour is pure Python-level shape handling in numpy.linalg._linalg, so it should reproduce on any platform that builds NumPy.
Dependency pins for pytest and hypothesis are unbounded in the evidence; the strategy chose current versions from pip, and this choice is not an era-documented constraint.

oracle.reference_source: developer regression test assert res.shape == (4,) in test_regression.py
oracle.why: Shape is an exact integer comparison, so no numerical tolerance applies.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On the buggy revision, array-valued rtol is not broadcast to the batch shape (4,), so the tolerance computation does not yield one tolerance per stacked matrix; the returned result does not have shape (4,) (or the broadcast fails), so assert res.shape == (4,) raises AssertionError for the array cases.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: With rtol = broadcast_to(rtol, A.shape[:-2])[..., newaxis], each rtol element maps to one stacked matrix, the result has shape (4,), and the assertion holds for all three parameterizations.
